content: Task Model v3 orchestrator half is unimplemented: no write surface for plan/assignee/depends_on, and fleet-scope slices are invisible to workers. Measured 2026-10-18 by the morning-pass run (cycle 12970). EVIDENCE: (1) task_upsert() has 20 args, NO p_plan (pg_get_function_arguments); task-db.py has no --plan; v009 §1 + docs/design/task-model-v3.md P3 both REQUIRE orchestrator-written plans. 12 of 19 open slices have plan IS NULL. (2) ssh mosesaaron: moses' tasks DB contains 0 of esther's 16 pending fleet slices (only 2 personal ones); task-db.py prints 'stored LOCALLY on this host only'. (3) 0 of 19 open slices have assignee or correlation_id; all worker inboxes depth 0 -> the bus dispatch path had never fired. (4) add hardwires p_depends_on=None, so the cost chain (slices 40cb307d/511ad057 'waiting') cannot be machine-gated - the very gap tracked as blocked slice 2fc4d871. FIX DIRECTION (needs adversarial review before building, per Luke's standing rule): (a) add --plan to task-db.py add/update and thread p_plan through task_upsert; (b) add an orchestrator hand-out surface (--assignee / --depends-on on update, or a dispatch helper that sets assignee + correlation_id and sends the bus TASK_REQUEST atomically) so a handed-out slice is machine-visible; (c) until (b) ships, the morning pass must dispatch via the bus (hc send <agent> TASK_REQUEST, proven working 2026-10-18: ca282975 -> joseph, msg_id ae11d3bb, landed inbox_joseph depth 1) rather than pretending pull-claim works. Do NOT write plans by raw SQL - that bypasses the single write path.

PII gate false positive: the write-time phone-shape pattern (governance-enforcer, two-separator national form) matches three dashed digit groups inside a UUID, so writing a verbatim psql row containing a session UUID into the repo is refused as 'phone number'. Hit 2026-10-16 while writing docs/evidence/backlog-run-2026-10-16-selection.md (the row had to be tail-elided, and the raw refusal came from write_file). Evidence: the file's section 4 records the elision and why. Fix direction: exclude a match that sits inside a hex/UUID token (e.g. require the whole match not be flanked by hex digits), then verify with the enforcer's own test fixtures plus a differential case for this shape (tests/test_enforcer_pii_gate.py).
STORY: Fleet cost under $10/day avg + halve review queue (HC gaps party 2026-08-21 roadmap)

[queue/1] Return the 18 session-TTL parked rows to a decided state (queue reduction 18 to 0). Source: the 2026-10 review-queue diagnosis doc, remedy 2. Re-measured 2026-10-16: the paused class is STILL exactly 18 rows, unchanged since the 2026-10-14 diagnosis, i.e. the named remedy has sat unowned for 2 days. All 18 are project=hermes-cortex, priority=0, untrusted=true (minted from inbound PROPOSAL/ISSUES content). The return arc is already legal by migration v012 (parked rows return to pool). Executable plan: (1) read the 18 rows (task list filtered status paused) and classify each by content as real-work versus untrusted-junk proposal; (2) decide per row WITHOUT unattended destruction: real-work rows go back to status pending; junk rows are NOT cancelled unattended - escalate that batch to Luke with the list and a recommendation, per the destructive-default no-op rule; (3) execute the pending returns one row at a time; (4) re-measure: paused count must reach 0, record the claimable-pool delta as a before/after table; (5) if any returned row is claimable, the resume routine (remedy 3) is a SEPARATE slice, not this one. Evidence required: before/after census plus the 60-65 minute dwell signature. Owner: orchestrator - local-store write, cannot be delegated because fleet rows live on the orchestrator host only.

Reflexion gate is unsatisfiable for a cron/bg session that lacks the skill_view tool: hc-reflexion-check.py answers only from mycortex_mem.tool_events, which the enforcer hook writes when Hermes invokes skill_view, so such a session cannot satisfy the gate and its evidence can never be committed (measured twice: 2026-10-12 per DOCS-INDEX row 107 / loop-governance issue #95, and 2026-10-16 in docs/evidence/briefings/BLOCKER-reflexion-gate-skill_view-2026-10-16.md). Fix direction (that blocker's option 2): give the gate an explicit, audited path for automated sessions that records an honest artefact marker (e.g. 'cron session - check answered in docs/evidence/briefings/reflexion-check-<date>.md') instead of requiring a tool the session does not have. Do NOT satisfy it by fabricating a tool_events row.

Root cause of the [queue/2] mis-projection class: task-db.py add defaults project to 'hermes-cortex' when --project is omitted, so every slice minted with --parent but no explicit project lands in the orchestrator's own project regardless of the parent story's project. Found 2026-10-16 while correcting 7 such slices (evidence: docs/evidence/slice-project-reproject-2026-10-16.txt). Fix direction: when --parent <story-id> is given and --project is omitted, inherit the parent row's project instead of the hardcoded default; keep the hardcoded default only for parentless rows. Verify with a unit test that adds a child under a kaesa story and asserts project=kaesa-90day. Note the second half of the same gap: --depends_on still has no update surface (tracked on 2fc4d871).

Task-mint path creates duplicate and contentless task rows from inbox traffic (measured 2026-10-19 by the orch-bus-worker pass). Evidence: the residual paused class of 10 rows all carry a bare-token content ('ISSUES'/'PROPOSAL', no body); 5 of them coincide within 3-7 s with DOCTOR_TEST e2e self-test messages in the moses bus archive, 2 are proven self-test PROPOSALs ('self-test: bare PROPOSAL must not error' cycle 10250; 'SELFTEST skill-content request flow for titus'), and 3 are near-timestamped duplicates of rows already returned to pending on 2026-10-17 (c05e2c78, ed4b4c43). The mint consumes self-test traffic, drops the message body (content=subject only) and mints a second bare row per message. Consequence: 6 of the 8 rows returned to pending by the 10-17 queue/1 remedy are still unactionable bare-token rows (f3034287, a173cb3f, e60f338a, c05e2c78, ed4b4c43, 0a239ef6). Fix direction (needs adversarial review before building, per Luke's standing rule): (1) skip self-test subjects (DOCTOR_TEST, SELFTEST, 'self-test:') in the inbox->task mint; (2) de-duplicate on (source message subject + body hash) so one inbound message mints one task; (3) carry the message body into the task content instead of the bare subject. Verification: assert one task per archived message over a fixture batch containing a DOCTOR_TEST and a PROPOSAL pair, and assert no row is minted with content shorter than its subject plus a body.

Broken skill references: repo skills/devops/llm-cost-optimization/SKILL.md cites 4 reference files that do NOT exist in the repo (fleet-cost-data-sources, interactive-session-cost-state-db, openrouter-model-catalogue, session-telemetry-reporting); they exist only in the deployed skill tree. The cost-removal sweep commit 093b993d deleted 3 of them from the repo but left the SKILL.md References list intact; 2 more were never committed. Reader impact measured 2026-10-15: the deployed fleet-cost-data-sources.md presents orch-daily-cost-report.py and cron-costs.db as live, but both were removed 2026-10-06 — this misled the backlog pass into believing a cost-report cron still exists. Same class as f97dcffe (deployed-only files): resolve the prune-vs-restore decision THERE rather than racing it here. Evidence: git log --all -- skills/devops/llm-cost-optimization/references/<file>.md; repo references/ has 4 files vs deployed 9.

[cost/2] Reduce top cost drivers: from baseline doc, cut duplicated cron runs / over-spec models per cron; apply provider/pin changes in env vars (single control point), measure delta over 7 days. Output: docs/cost-reduction-2026-09.md with before/after table. Depends on [cost/1].

[cost/1] Baseline fleet cost: query provider spend + token usage for last 14 days across all agents; produce per-agent, per-cron cost table; identify top 3 cost drivers. Output: docs/cost-baseline-2026-09.md in shared repo.

[queue/3] Populate depends_on for the cost-slice chain so waiting is machine-readable. Source: docs/review-queue-diagnosis-2026-10.md remedy #6. [cost/2]=40cb307d and [cost/3]=511ad057 sit in waiting on [cost/1]=5e875477, but depends_on is EMPTY on all four cost rows - the dependency exists only in the prose of the task body, so no query can see it and nothing can auto-resume when [cost/1] completes. Executable plan: (1) confirm the intended chain cost/1 -> cost/2 -> cost/3 with the story owner; (2) set depends_on on 40cb307d and 511ad057; (3) verify with a read that filters on depends_on that both rows are found from cost/1; (4) if no update path exposes depends_on (same gap as [queue/2]), record the tool gap and stop. Explicit non-goal: do NOT add auto-resume automation here - moving a row when its blocker clears is a pipeline change (scope-crossing, skill task-queue-workflow) and must be a separately-approved cycle, not an unattended cron action. Owner: orchestrator.

test_task_queue_evidence.py::test_the_committed_evidence_is_actual_script_output is RED and invoker-dependent: it spawns 'python3 ops/scripts/manage/task-queue-evidence.py', and that python3 is the agent runtime interpreter with no pytest, so the script's output differs from the committed evidence. Fails identically at HEAD and at baseline 40151607 (1 failed, 8 passed in 1.71s in the detached worktree), so it predates the 2026-10-16 hermeticity fix to test_task_db_unit.py. Same class as ebe4e9d8: a probe whose verdict depends on the interpreter/cwd of whoever invoked it. Fix direction: resolve the interpreter by CAPABILITY (ops/scripts/lib/python-with-module.sh pytest) inside the test's subprocess call, or make the evidence script emit its output independently of the caller's python3. Evidence: docs/evidence/task-db-scoped-query-hermetic-2026-10-16.txt sections 5 and 7 (cycle 12745).

Briefing pipeline: verify_briefing.py is never run against DELIVERED briefings, so the canonical format contract drifted unnoticed - briefings 2026-10-09 through 10-15 fail their own checker (0 line-start 'Source:' lines, 1450-1750 words vs the 600-1200 contract) and nothing surfaced it. Measured 2026-10-16 by the sustainability-briefing pass: probe output in docs/evidence/briefings/checker-drift-probe-2026-10-16.txt (2026-10-08 canonical: ALL PASS; 2026-10-09 and 10-12: FAILURES; 2026-10-16 restored: ALL PASS). Fix direction: make the daily briefing job run the canonical checker on what it delivers and refuse (or flag) a deliverable that fails, so the drift cannot recur silently. Standing rule as a gate, not prose (SOUL P6).

[cost/3] Continuous cost monitoring: add per-cron token/spend tag to metrics sink :14005 and a weekly cost-report cron with alert when fleet daily avg exceeds $10; verify alert fires once in test. Depends on [cost/1].

MORNING-PASS REPORTING DEFECT: three different 'claimable' counts from one task store. Measured 2026-10-19 by the morning task pass (read-only; no cycle). (a) task-db.py list --board prints 'pending (claimable): 31' because its classifier labels EVERY pending non-story row claimable (task-db.py ~line 953: kind='story' -> 'not claimable', ELSE -> 'claimable'), so ~15 kind=NULL rows (PROPOSAL/ISSUES/personal dev tasks) are counted as worker-claimable; (b) list --claimable prints 16 - the correct v3 pool (status=pending AND kind='slice' AND assignee IS NULL, cmd_list_claimable) - but ONLY when --limit 50 is passed: the default limit is 10 AND the view prints no '...N more' notice, so this pass first read '10 claimable' from a silently truncated list; (c) the cron prompt in ops/install/cron-manifest.yaml step 1 says 'list --claimable' with no limit, so every morning pass inherits the truncation and any report quoting that number under-reports the pool by 6. Fix direction: (1) print a truncation notice (or the true total) whenever the pool exceeds --limit; (2) make the board label match the pool definition, or print both numbers; (3) decide whether kind=NULL rows should ever be claimable; (4) change the manifest prompt to 'list --claimable --limit 50'. Evidence: the three command outputs as captured in the 2026-10-19 morning-pass session.

Detector gap: stranded-skill detection covers SKILL.md only - extend check-skill-drift-parity.py to SUPPORT files under repo-owned skill dirs. Measured 2026-10-15 by the orch-bus-worker pass: 131 deployed-only files across 386 repo-owned skill dirs (e.g. devops/enforcement-gate-migration/references+//templates, devops/auto-remediation/references/, devops/loop-governance/references/, software-development/change-checklist/references/). The deploy guardrail refuses to overwrite deployed copies, so these never reach the fleet. Fix direction: walk references/, templates/, scripts/ under repo-owned skill dirs with the same content-not-mtime direction rule, then decide the 131 by content (many may be deliberately repo-ahead). Evidence: docs/evidence/stranded-skills-reconcile-2026-10-15.txt (cycle 12652).
